title: Reduction square for the compact-support projection
statement:
Fix the normalized descent maps and presentations [def-sp-complete-projection-descent-maps]. For any compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow Z,p:Z\to Y)$ of $f$, any normalized reduction/limit presentations on $X,Z,Y$, and arbitrary integral derived modules $M$ on $X$ and $K$ on $Y$, put $H=M\otimes f^*K$. Assume only that the inverse open system projection at $(r_XM,G_p r_YK)$ is invertible. Let $\pi_R:F_RM\otimes K\to F_RH$ be the actual integral compact-support projection [def-pur-integral-ringed-projection-maps], $\theta$ the system projection, $b_N$ the reconstruction map, $\mu$ the tensor/scalar isomorphism, and $\nu_f$ the pullback/scalar isomorphism, all as defined by the descent maps. Then the square
$$r_Y(\pi_R);b_H;F_\bullet(\mu_{M,f^*K};(1\otimes\nu_{f,K}))=\mu_{F_RM,K};(b_M\otimes1);\theta$$
commutes as an equality of whole derived coefficient-system morphisms. Composition is written in order of application. No completeness, boundedness, finite-type condition, proper-projection invertibility, or invertibility of the reconstruction maps is assumed.

source.place: Paragraphs (2)-(3), normalized comparisons and projection descent

proof.text:
The specified tensor and pullback models identify the derived comparisons on whole quotient complexes with the canonical scalar-extension maps: both send every pure tensor quotient augmentation to the same two augmentation generators, and the recorded representative squares descend this equality. Put $Z=\bar X$ and let $q_T$ be the ringed sequence projection defining $r_T$, for $T=Z,Y$. For the commutative square with vertical edges $p:Z\to Y$, $p_\bullet:Z^{\mathbf N}\to Y^{\mathbf N}$ and horizontal edges $q_Z,q_Y$, let $h_B:r_YRp_{*,R}B\to Rp_{*,\bullet}r_ZB$ be the mate of the canonical pullback square. In particular $h_B$ is the transpose under $Lp_\bullet^*\dashv Rp_{*,\bullet}$ of $r_Z$ of the proper counit, after $\nu_p$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to this square, with arbitrary $B\in D(R_Z)$ and $K\in D(R_Y)$. It gives
$$Rp_{*,\bullet}(a^p_{B,K})h_{B\otimes^LLp_R^*K}\,r_Y(\pi^p_R)=\pi^p_\bullet(h_B\otimes1)\mu_{Rp_{*,R}B,K},$$
where $a^p=(1\otimes\nu_p)\mu$. This is an equality in the derived category of systems, for the counit-defined projections $\pi^p$; the cited theorem allows arbitrary ringed topoi and arbitrary structural ring maps. No invertibility of $h$ or $\pi^p$ is used here.

source.place: Paragraph (3), compatibility of the proper counit projection with reduction

proof.text:
Let $d_N:r_Zj_{!,R}N\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{!,\bullet}r_XN$ be the canonical open scalar comparison. The localized ringed-site and ringed-diagram assertions of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] apply to the constant sequence ring $\Delta R_Z\to A_{\bullet,Z}$ and its restriction to $X$. On quotient representatives $d$ is $[x]\otimes a\mapsto[x\otimes a|_X]$. It carries the open unit to the system open unit: after restriction both sides are $x\otimes a\mapsto x\otimes a$. This identity is simultaneous in the quotient diagram by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; the scalar tensor and restriction comparisons are $\mu,\nu$ of the specified presentation.

Write $\gamma_R:j_!N\otimes^LJ\to j_!(N\otimes^Lj^*J)$ and $\gamma_\bullet$ for the inverse-unit open projection maps. Their inverses are the open adjuncts of unit tensor identity by [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Taking these adjuncts, the two routes in
$$j_{!,\bullet}(a^j_{N,J})\,d_{N\otimes^Lj^*J}\,r_Z(\gamma_R)=\gamma_\bullet(d_N\otimes1)\mu_{j_!N,J}$$
restrict to the same unit tensor identity, by the displayed formula for $d$ and the unit-compatible $\mu,\nu$. The open adjunction Hom bijection therefore gives the equality before evaluating the systems. Here $a^j=(1\otimes\nu_j)\mu$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), compatibility of the inverse open unit projection with reduction

proof.text:
For $N=M,H:=M\otimes^Lf_R^*K$, denote the defined compactification/limit map by $\alpha_N:F_RN\to L_YF_\bullet r_XN$. Its reconstruction transpose is
$$b_N=e_{F_\bullet r_XN}\,r_Y(\alpha_N):r_YF_RN\longrightarrow F_\bullet r_XN.$$
We check which comparison this is. The defining normalization writes $\alpha_N$ as $Rp_{*,R}j_{!,R}(\eta_N)$ followed by the open/limit and proper/limit comparisons and scalar restrictions. The proper/limit comparison is the direct-image composition comparison for $pq_Z=q_Yp_\bullet$; by [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] that composition comparison is adjunction-compatible. Its conjugate is the proper mate $h$ in the first step. The open/limit comparison is conjugate to $d$ in the open step: its transpose is the open scalar map whose restriction is the same open unit, hence equals $d$ by the open adjunction Hom bijection. Pasting these squares by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], and cancelling $L_X(e)\eta_{L_X}=1$ and $e_{r_X}r_X(\eta)=1$, gives
$$b_N=Rp_{*,\bullet}(d_N)\,h_{j_{!,R}N}.$$
These cancellations use the actual reduction/limit adjunction of the specified presentation. Thus this is the comparison specified in the question, not an identification inferred only from finite projections.

source.place: Paragraphs (2)-(3), normalization by the compactification/limit comparisons and reconstruction counits

proof.text:
Apply the proper step with $B=j_{!,R}M$ and the open step with $N=M$, $J=Lp_R^*K$, using $j^*Lp_R^*K\cong Lf_R^*K$. The canonical pullback-composition comparisons are monoidal and adjunction-compatible by [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], so $a^j,a^p$ combine to the specified scalar tensor/pullback identification for $H$. Compose the proper equality with $Rp_{*,\bullet}$ of the open equality. Naturality of $h$ moves $\gamma_R$ past $h$; the reconstruction-transpose step then identifies each $Rp_{*,\bullet}(d_N)h_{j_!N}$ with $b_N$. The result is
$$b_H\,r_Y(\pi_R)=\theta\,(b_M\otimes1)\mu_{F_RM,K},$$
with the input tensor/pullback coordinates understood. This is the displayed square before any inverse reconstruction coordinate is introduced. It therefore does not require reconstruction invertibility or completeness.
